# Model Mountain — three-minute demonstration

1. Problem (20 s): A business assistant can receive malicious documents and tool text.
   Show the intended audience and the limits of a model-only defense.
2. Request workflow (45 s): Ask a benign policy question, then a prompt-injection or
   unauthorized action. Show source citations, withheld output and the independent
   authorization boundary. State whether this run is CPU simulation or real inference.
3. Model internals (45 s): Select a compatible remote model. Show runtime/model revision,
   capture and vector provenance, then a genuinely captured direction and hook evidence.
   If remote work is blocked, show the exact blocker instead of simulated measurements.
4. Evaluation (40 s): Compare A/B/C/D on held-out cases. Show attack successes, false
   refusals, incorrect answers, unknown/time-out counts, latency and adverse outcomes.
   Explain that string matching is only a proxy and classifier accuracy is not causality.
5. Feasibility and next steps (30 s): Vercel web/API, Kaggle GPU boundary, model/runtime
   constraints, privacy, accessibility and practical scope. Show the live Model Mountain
   task status and the contribution/AI-tool disclosure. Finish with measured limits.
